text:
maria (netops): FYI, seeing a pattern of DNS failures from multiple edge clusters (apac/eu-west) starting ~07:40 UTC. services intermittently get NXDOMAIN or >300ms resolve times, triggering retries and causing model-pull/backoff on GPU nodes. not service-wide but noisy across several AZs.

kevin (sre): any correlation with NAT/gateway change or recent egress scaling?

maria (netops): no infra deploys during window. looked at host resolver traces — many duplicated queries to upstream due to stub resolver retrying. suspect port exhaustion / src-port rotation issue on NATs causing retries to hit different upstreams.

li (edge): can you paste sample `resolv.conf` and `ss` output? some AMIs recently switched from systemd-resolved to glibc stub behavior, might explain different ndots handling.

maria (netops): here you go. `resolv.conf` from affected node:
```
nameserver 10.20.0.2
options timeout:1 attempts:2 rotate
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local
```
`ss -u -n sport = :53 | wc -l` -> 14200
`ss -s` shows high udp sockets in TIME-WAIT-like states (ephemeral).

andrew (infra): 14k sockets is a lot. check conntrack and nat ephemeral ports on the NAT instance. run `conntrack -L | grep DNS` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`.

maria (netops): conntrack hits ~85% of max (65536), ip_local_port_range is `32768 60999`. conntrack shows many ESTABLISHED/RELATED for udp dport 53.

kevin (sre): that explains fanout. When source ports reuse/rotate poorly, the stub resolver retries create duplicate upstream queries because replies get dropped or mapped to wrong socket. For short timeouts (timeout:1 attempts:2) you get query thundering. In busy workload with small src port space NAT can map collisions.

li (edge): quick mitigations:
- increase conntrack max and timeout for RELATED UDP flows
- expand ip_local_port_range to use full ephemeral space (e.g., 10240-65535)
- add per-node DNS caching (nscd/dnsmasq) on edge host to collapse fanout
- temporary: bump resolver `timeout` to 2 and attempts to 3 in `resolv.conf` to reduce retry storms

maria (netops): rolling the following on a small canary:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 65535"
systemctl restart dnsmasq # run locally with cache-size=1000
```
monitoring: conntrack dips to ~40% after change, socket counts drop.

ops-bot: deploy started by maria (netops) — canary group: edge-apac-1 (5 nodes).

kevin (sre): also saw upstream recursive servers returning SERVFAIL briefly; probably overloaded by duplicate queries. we should add fallback resolvers in region (secondary) and push aggressive TTL caching at dnsmasq to prevent repeated queries for same prefix.

andrew (infra): for long-term: investigate NAT64/44 translator settings in cloud router (source port randomization/syn policy). Open ticket to provider: they have a config for port-preservation vs randomization that affects reuse.

maria (netops): filed ticket #INF-4621 with provider, included pcap snippet and conntrack dump. provider response: "investigating high ephemeral port reuse under burst UDP flows".

sre-oncall: what's the impact on latency SLOs? need to assess customer-facing degradation for dedicated clusters.

maria (netops): internal metric: 2% of requests saw >200ms DNS latency, 0.4% NXDOMAIN spikes leading to retries and 0.1% 5xx errors on model endpoints. so noticeable but contained.

li (edge): short checklist to apply everywhere ASAP:
- widen ip_local_port_range
- raise conntrack limit + tune `nf_conntrack_udp_timeout` to 30
- deploy dnsmasq/local cache on every edge host (cache size 2k, negative cache TTL 30s)
- add second regional resolver and mark it lower priority; ensure `rotate` in resolv.conf is present

kevin (sre): add a guardrail to autoscaler so provisioning doesn't exacerbate (spinning up many new pods causes resolver storm). maybe stagger startup or prewarm DNS cache with `getent hosts` for critical domains.

maria (netops): notes from canary: implementing above reduced DNS retries by ~92% and upstream SERVFAILs disappeared. rolling to eu-west canary next.

andrew (infra): follow-up items:
- provider ticket (#INF-4621) track and collect NAT metrics
- run e2e test that simulates high-concurrency UDP DNS queries from edge nodes (script in infra/playbooks/dns-fanout-test)
- add proactive alert if `ss -u` sockets > 5k per node or conntrack > 70%

li (edge): config snippets we used: 
```
# /etc/dnsmasq.conf
cache-size=2000
neg-ttl=30
listen-address=127.0.0.1

# resolv.conf fragment we push via cloud-init
nameserver 127.0.0.1
nameserver 10.20.0.2
options timeout:2 attempts:3 rotate ndots:1
```

maria (netops): thanks everyone. rolling to eu-west and then global after provider update. will post a brief incident note once provider confirms root cause. (reaction :thumbsup:)

ops-bot: canary roll complete for edge-apac-1. all checks green.

kevin (sre): nice work. add a note to run the dns-fanout-test in pre-merge for large infra changes that affect resolver behavior.

sre-oncall: monitoring rules created: alert if per-node UDP sockets > 5000 or conntrack usage > 70% for 5m.

maria (netops): closing loop — provider confirmed: port allocation policy on their NAT gateway had a bug that reduced usable ephemeral pool under bursty UDP flows. they deployed a fix at 09:12 UTC. our mitigations remain in place as defense in depth.
